reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it invites its audience to register for a named trading account and explicitly prompts them to join. It instructs participants to send Bitcoin, submit a transaction ID and payment proof, and move an activation-wallet balance into a trading pool. It also requests identity information and displays paid percentage-based trading bonuses, although the available video evidence does not establish that any transaction, payout, identity verification, or displayed result was completed or genuine.

citations.quote: How To Register And Fund Your MTI Account
You will need the referral link of the person who invited you to join Mirror Trading International
Make the payment by sending the bitcoin.
If your Bitcoin is in your Activation Wallet then click on the Add Funds To Pool
Each day you will receive a statement via email telling you the results of the trades.

opening.argument: The material describes an account process and reporting, not a promised outcome: it says members receive statements describing trading results, without guaranteeing profit or a return. It also directs registrants to read and accept terms and conditions before registration. A careful judge should distinguish explaining how an account works from claiming that its results are certain. The supplied evidence does not establish that the displayed figures were paid out, or that the tutorial represents them as guaranteed.

citations.quote: Each day you will receive a statement via email telling you the results of the trades.
Read the terms and conditions and then click I have read and accepted the terms and conditions.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's cited steps establish that the tutorial explains a funding workflow, but not that it promises returns or conceals uncertainty. A Bitcoin payment and a statement about trading results do not, by themselves, establish what those results will be or that the viewer will profit. Its own qualification that no payout or displayed result is verified underscores this evidentiary limit.

citations.quote: Make the payment by sending the bitcoin.
Each day you will receive a statement via email telling you the results of the trades.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a guaranteed-profit sentence does not change the tutorial's practical invitation: it tells viewers how to fund a trading pool with Bitcoin and says they will receive trading-result statements. The terms checkbox is a registration step, not a risk warning. The opening's careful limitation about unverified outcomes does not erase the pool-funded trading proposition presented to prospective participants.

citations.quote: click on the Add Funds To Pool
Each day you will receive a statement via email telling you the results of the trades.

opening.argument: This is structured as an operational walkthrough: it explains registration, profile updates, payment submission, and where to view account statements. The title itself describes registering and funding an account, and the narration proceeds through interface steps rather than making a market forecast or asserting a particular profit. Showing how an interface is used is not the same as proving the service is legitimate, but neither does the supplied material establish that the tutorial is a deceptive claim about returns. Its primary demonstrated content is account operation.

citations.quote: How To Register And Fund Your MTI Account
Now that you have your login details, please log in to the BACK office at mymticlub.com.
Click on the view option to see your daily statement.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution points to joining, Bitcoin funding, and pool transfers, but those are also the steps this operational tutorial sets out to demonstrate. The title and narration identify account registration and funding as the subject; they do not assert a guaranteed return. A closing invitation does not alone establish that the explanatory material makes a false claim about the service's performance.

citations.quote: How To Register And Fund Your MTI Account
The amount of Bitcoin you want to transfer from your activation wallet will show, and all you need to do is click on submit.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough is not merely neutral interface education: it tells viewers to register through an inviter's link, send Bitcoin, and move funds into a trading pool, then ends with an explicit invitation to join. That sequence promotes participation in a Bitcoin-funded trading arrangement whose stated purpose includes trading results. Calling it a tutorial does not remove that promotional function.

citations.quote: You will need the referral link of the person who invited you to join Mirror Trading International
Make the payment by sending the bitcoin.

opening.argument: The video can be read as a service-registration and payment tutorial: it shows account fields, a payment-information screen, and submission of a transaction ID and proof of payment. Those are concrete account-administration steps, not proof of a fraudulent mechanism. The supplied material does not state a guaranteed return, explain that referrals earn income, or establish that any depicted balance or bonus was actually received. It also directs users to accept terms before registering. The evidence therefore supports describing a promoted account workflow, but not concluding from these steps alone that the workflow is a scam.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution emphasizes Bitcoin transfers and an activation-wallet-to-pool step, but these show how the account workflow operates, not that a return is guaranteed or that a referral pays income. The cited daily statements report trading results; they do not specify a promised rate. Even the visible bonus report cannot establish that a participant's deposit caused those entries or that the entries were paid out.

citations.quote: If your Bitcoin is in your Activation Wallet then click on the Add Funds To Pool
Each day you will receive a statement via email telling you the results of the trades.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: This is more than ordinary payment administration: the instructions explicitly direct a Bitcoin payment and then a transfer into a trading pool, while describing daily trading results and showing a trading-bonus report. The fact that the material does not prove a payout or state a guaranteed rate limits what can be claimed about outcomes, but it does not make the promoted pool relationship ordinary retail commerce.
